content: Serutan was a product heavily advertised on radio and television from the 1930s through the 1960s. It was manufactured by the J.B. Williams Company, which was established in 1885 and later acquired by Nabisco in 1971. The origin of the brand name was quite straightforward: the creators simply spelled the word natures backward. The advertising slogan for the product was Read it backwards, emphasizing its natural qualities. This was intended to distinguish it from other laxative brands that relied on chemical stimulation of the colon rather than the bulk-forming action of its contents. The product was predominantly marketed on programs with a core audience that demographic studies showed to be significantly older than the average television viewer. Serutan is particularly associated with The Lawrence Welk Show and The Original Amateur Hour, both of which were also sponsored by other J.B. Williams products, such as Sominex, a sleeping aid, and Geritol, a vitamin supplement. During the 1930s and 1940s, Serutan became the subject of numerous jokes by radio comedians. Additionally, the term Serutan Approach has been used in the context of the positivist definition of science, reflecting a broader trend in scientific methodology.
